```json { "title": "HOA Fence Staining in Northern Colorado: Why Prep and Process Matter", "meta_description": "See how Keystone Painting handled this HOA-approved fence staining project in Northern Colorado with solid stain application and professional prep work.", "content": "

We recently wrapped up a fence staining project in Northern Colorado where the homeowner needed HOA approval before we could touch a single board. That's standard for most neighborhoods in Timnath, Severance, Windsor, and Fort Collins—your HOA controls exterior color choices, whether it's your house or your fence. The project involved converting the fence from a semi-transparent stain to a solid stain, a darker color that the HOA specifically approved. It's a perfect example of how the right prep process, the right product choice, and experienced crews make the difference between a paint job that lasts and one that doesn't.

What We Did

Our crew showed up early to mask everything that didn't need stain—we're talking hardware, neighbor properties, landscaping. You protect what matters before you spray. We raked back the rocks at the base of the fence so we could restage the landscape without any discoloration afterward. That's detail work that separates contractors who think ahead from ones who don't.

The application itself was a two-step process. We sprayed the fence with a 410 tip—that reduces overspray and keeps the application controlled. Then we back-rolled it. Two to three guys working together, each knowing their role. We started at 9 a.m. and wrapped inside an hour. This was a heavy application of solid stain, the kind that requires coordination and experience to get right.

Why Prep Matters More Than Paint

Here's what most homeowners don't realize: the fence stain is only as good as the surface it's going on. We could've skipped the masking, the rock raking, the careful layout—and saved an hour of labor. The stain would still look decent for a month. But it wouldn't last. Solid stain protects longer than semi-transparent because it has denser UV protection. That protection only works if the surface is prepped right and the application is consistent.

That's why we talk to every Northern Colorado customer about HOA approval first. Get the color locked in before we quote. Get us involved early if you're not sure about the process. We've worked with HOAs across the region long enough to know what slides through and what doesn't. Licensed, insured, $1M liability—we know what we're doing because we've done thousands of jobs like this.

The Result

A fence that won't fade fast, that's HOA-approved, and that was installed by a crew that knew exactly what they were doing. Solid stain lasts longer than semi-transparent. It handles Northern Colorado's sun, wind, and temperature swings better. The homeowner gets longevity and curb appeal without having to worry about whether the job was cut corners on or done right.

If you've got a fence, deck, or exterior surface in Northern Colorado and you're thinking about staining it, get your HOA approval sorted first—then call us for a quote. We'll walk you through the process, tell you which products actually protect your investment, and get it done right the first time.

faqs.q: What's involved in preparing a fence for staining in Northern Colorado?
faqs.a: Prep work is critical and includes masking off all adjacent surfaces, protecting your neighbor's property, and raking back landscaping at the base to prevent discoloration. We use a 410 tip spray application followed by back rolling to ensure even coverage and durability. For HOA-controlled communities like Timnath, Severance, Windsor, and Fort Collins, you'll need HOA color approval before we start—we can guide you through that process.

faqs.a: Fence staining projects typically range from $800 to $3,500+ depending on linear footage, existing condition, and whether you're upgrading to a solid stain for better UV protection and longevity. Your quote will include labor and materials unless it's a unique situation. Contact us at (970) 670-3965 for a free estimate based on your specific fence.

faqs.q: What's the difference between semi-transparent and solid fence stain, and why does Keystone Painting recommend solid?
faqs.a: Semi-transparent stain lets wood grain show through but requires more frequent reapplication. Solid stain provides denser UV protection and longer-lasting coverage—often the better choice for Northern Colorado's intense sun. If your HOA approves a solid color, you're getting superior protection and durability along with the aesthetic your community wants.

faqs.q: How does Keystone Painting protect my property and my neighbor's during exterior staining?
faqs.a: We mask off everything—hardware, trim, landscaping—and actively protect all adjacent property from overspray and stain contact. We rake back landscape material at the base so we can restore it without discoloration. Our crews work in teams of 2–3 people in concert with each other, ensuring quality application and site protection throughout the job.
